study_identification_part.si4_title: Brain-Charting Autism and Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Reveals Distinct and Overlapping Neurobiology

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To use population modeling on a large, multisite neuroimaging dataset (N = 4255) to characterize cortical anatomy associated with autism and ADHD, benchmarked against models of average brain development. The study also examined sex and age differences, the relationship with autistic traits, and the co-occurrence of autism and ADHD.

rci9_site_effect_handling.detail: ComBat was used to harmonize the data across all global and regional measures. Each site was treated as a batch, and covariates of age, sex, and diagnosis were included in the model to preserve related biological variation. The ComBat-harmonized data was then used to generate the centile scores.
rci9_site_effect_handling.supporting_text: Due to the smaller sample sizes of some sites in our dataset and higher variability in the clinical samples, we /uniFB01 rst harmonized our data using ComBat (111), consistent with previous work (112). ComBat was applied to the entire dataset across all global and regional measures, with each site treated as a batch and with covariates of age, sex, and diagnosis to preserve related biological variation. ComBat-harmonized data were used as inputs to the out-of-sample maximum likelihood estimation to generate centile scores.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Multiple linear regressions were used to examine diagnostic group differences in centile scores, including sex-by-diagnosis and age-by-diagnosis interactions. All analyses were corrected for multiple comparisons using FDR and included Euler number and age as covariates. A priori sex-stratified analyses were also performed. Spearman correlations with spin permutation testing were used to compare the spatial similarity of effect size maps.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: The study identified distinct neuroanatomical signatures for autism (localized greater cortical thickness/volume in superior temporal cortex) and ADHD (global increases in thickness but lower volume/surface area), which were differentially modulated by sex and age, with a unique pattern for co-occurring cases.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Autistic individuals showed greater cortical thickness (CT) and volume (CV) localized to the superior temporal gyrus (d=0.13-0.15) and larger ventricular volume. Individuals with ADHD showed widespread lower CV and surface area (SA) (d=-0.07 to -0.18) but globally greater mean CT (d=0.09). Sex modulated the neuroanatomy of autism (males drove the STG findings) but not ADHD. An age-by-diagnosis interaction was found for ADHD in frontal and parietal CT, but was limited for autism. The co-occurring autism+ADHD group showed a unique pattern of widespread significant increases in CT (d=0.10 to 0.24) and decreased SA in frontal/parietal regions.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: 1. Data were aggregated from multiple sources with different scanners and protocols; though harmonized, residual site effects and small effect sizes are concerns. 2. Cortical measures were averaged across hemispheres, precluding analysis of atypical asymmetry. 3. Lack of consistent phenotypic/diagnostic data across sites limited analyses of clinical correlations and co-occurring diagnoses. 4. The sample had imbalances in sex, IQ, support needs, and racial-ethnic diversity. 5. The study is cross-sectional, limiting inferences about developmental trajectories.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: Our results should be interpreted in light of some limitations. First, as is increasingly common, the data come from multiple sources, with different scanners, protocols, recruitment procedures, and demographic characteristics... we note that the effect sizes observed in most analyses were very small... Second, due to the availability of the models, cortical measures were averaged across hemispheres... Third, the lack of consistent phenotypic and diagnostic information led to limited data in the analyses of clinical measures and co-occurring diagnoses... Fourth, despite its large size, the representativeness of the sample is still suboptimal... Finally, the lack of longitudin...

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study uses a pre-trained normative model (BrainChart) to generate out-of-sample centile scores on a large, new dataset. This approach allows for benchmarking individual differences against a common reference, highlighting its utility for studying heterogeneity in and between clinical populations. Sensitivity analyses were conducted to test the robustness of the findings to different QC methods and harmonization strategies.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: A key finding is the divergent pattern of cortical alterations: autism effects were localized (superior temporal gyrus), whereas ADHD effects were more global, suggesting different underlying neurobiological mechanisms. The study also found that the neuroanatomical signature of co-occurring autism and ADHD was distinct from either condition alone, showing a pattern that resembled ADHD more than autism but with some unique features (e.g., widespread increased cortical thickness).
